issues.description: Attribute type mismatch for Course.ratings across artifacts: the problem statement (and the template) specify ratings as an array of Int, but the solution implementation declares ratings as [Double]. This discrepancy is structural (the collection element type differs) and will confuse students comparing the template/spec with the provided solution reference. It also changes the expected data shape when students implement addRating and getAverageRating.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution use the same element type as the problem statement and template. Either change solution_repository/Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift to declare ratings as [Int] (preferred to match the exercise text and template) and keep addRating(stars: Int) appending Ints, or update the problem statement and template to require [Double] and ensure all code/instructions reflect that. Prefer changing the solution to ratings: [Int] and computing the average as Double from Int sums.

issues.description: Inner-artifact type inconsistency inside the solution: in solution_repository/Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift ratings is declared as [Double], but addRating(stars:) appends an Int and getAverageRating uses an Int accumulator and adds rating values as if they were Int. These inconsistent uses of Int vs Double within the solution will cause type errors and make the reference implementation non-compilable/confusing.
issues.suggested_fix: Make types consistent within the solution implementation. For example, change ratings to var ratings: [Int] and keep addRating(stars: Int) appending Int values; in getAverageRating() sum Int ratings into an Int accumulator, then return Double(starSum) / Double(totalRatings) (with zero check). Alternatively, if you prefer Double ratings, convert stars to Double when appending and use Double accumulators everywhere. Ensure all operations use the same element type so the solution compiles and matches the intended exercise design.
